rewrites.title: Priming and rechallenge time course with chromatin accessibility readout
rewrites.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts, macrophages, or keratinocytes) to a transient AP-1-activating stimulus such as TPA, EGF, or wounding cues, wash it out, and rechallenge after days to weeks. Compare transcription and ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) in primed versus naive cells to determine whether response magnitude and kinetics persist after AP-1 activity has returned to baseline.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome with AP-1 motif activity inference across patient states
rewrites.description: Perform scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq on patient tissue or blood across disease stages, and compute chromVAR/SCENIC AP-1 activity and footprinting per cell. Test whether a stable AP-1-high subpopulation persists across time points or after treatment, and whether its accessible regions predict relapse or recall gene expression.

rewrites.title: Dose and sequence experiments distinguishing an integrator from a correlated readout
rewrites.description: Vary stimulus amplitude, duration, number of pulses, and inter-pulse interval, then test whether AP-1 occupancy predicts the later response better than the stimulus parameters do, i.e., whether AP-1 is a sufficient statistic that accounts for the input history. Pair this with mediation analysis and with partial AP-1 ablation at graded degrader doses to test whether response magnitude scales with the amount of AP-1 remaining.

rewrites.title: Hysteresis mapping with a live AP-1 reporter
rewrites.description: Using a live AP-1 activity reporter, drive cells up and then back down a graded stimulus dose (e.g., serum, TGF-beta, stiffness, or an optogenetic FOS/JUN input). Test whether the up- and down-going dose-response curves separate into a hysteresis loop with a bistable region rather than retracing each other. This distinguishes a self-sustaining memory state from slow first-order relaxation, which a persistence-duration experiment cannot do.

rewrites.title: Lineage-resolved memory tracing across divisions
rewrites.description: Combine CRISPR lineage barcodes with a recorder of prior AP-1 activity, such as a Fos-promoter-driven recombinase or stable reporter, and follow clonal lineages through several divisions. Use single-cell multiome readouts to test whether the primed state is inherited within clones, and whether it is uniform or confined to a subpopulation.

rewrites.title: Base-editing of AP-1 motifs at endogenous primed enhancers
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR base editors or prime editors to mutate the TRE/AP-1 motifs in 3 to 5 enhancers that show memory-like priming, then compare primed-state accessibility and re-stimulation kinetics in edited versus control clones. This tests whether the specific motif sites, rather than general AP-1 presence, carry the memory. Estimated cost is about $9k to $14k for guide design, clone isolation, and ATAC/RNA readouts.

rewrites.title: Motif-level CRISPR editing plus synthetic AP-1 recruitment
rewrites.description: Delete or mutate AP-1 motifs at specific memory enhancers and test whether priming is lost. Conversely, recruit AP-1 to a neutral locus with dCas9 and test whether this creates a persistent, restimulation-competent state. This tests necessity and sufficiency at the locus level.

rewrites.title: Meta-analysis of AP-1 motif enrichment at persistently open sites across systems
rewrites.description: Gather public before/during/after chromatin datasets from multiple memory paradigms (inflammatory memory, trained immunity, wound healing, senescence, drug-tolerant persisters, T-cell exhaustion, activity-dependent neuronal enhancers). Classify induced chromatin sites as persistent or transient, then test whether AP-1 motifs are enriched at persistent sites compared with transient sites matched for GC content, induction strength, and baseline accessibility. The matching controls for AP-1 motifs being common at enhancers in general.

rewrites.title: Single-cell tracking of AP-1 history through divisions
rewrites.description: Combine a live AP-1 activity reporter (e.g., a destabilized fluorescent protein under an AP-1-responsive or Fos promoter) with lineage barcodes and single-cell multiome readout. Compare cells with different prior AP-1 histories to test whether the prior state is inherited by daughter cells and predicts their later response, which separates heritable memory from stochastic cell-to-cell variation.

rewrites.title: Heritability estimation with lineage barcodes
rewrites.description: Use lineage barcoding (e.g., Rewind or ClonMapper) to track sister and cousin cells across several divisions after a stimulus, and calculate how strongly AP-1 target accessibility and expression correlate within each lineage. If within-clone correlation decays slowly across generations, and more slowly than for non-AP-1 programs, this is evidence that AP-1 carries a heritable state.

rewrites.title: Synthetic sufficiency test by targeted AP-1 recruitment
rewrites.description: Recruit a Fos/Jun bZIP effector to defined candidate memory enhancers with dCas9 without any stimulus, then withdraw recruitment and assay whether primed behavior appears days later. Complement this with base-edited destruction of individual endogenous AP-1 motifs to test necessity for maintenance separately from necessity for the acute response.

rewrites.title: Serial-passage test of AP-1-induced state propagation
rewrites.description: Stimulate a culture, then passage cells through many divisions without stimulus, sampling at intervals for chromatin accessibility and transcription at AP-1 targets. Persistence across passages, compared with lineage-matched controls and AP-1 knockouts, would indicate heritable memory rather than a transient response.

rewrites.title: Cross-stimulus priming with orthogonal pathway controls
rewrites.description: Prime cells with two or more stimuli that converge on AP-1 through different upstream routes (e.g., phorbol ester, EGF, or a stress stimulus), then cross-challenge each. Include MEK inhibitor and NF-kB or STAT inhibitor arms and profile their target genes, to test whether the memory encodes stimulus identity specifically and is AP-1-dependent rather than a generic activation signature.

rewrites.title: Tracking the primed state through mitosis and replication
rewrites.description: Combine clonal barcoding with division counting (dye dilution or FUCCI-gated sorting) and single-cell multiome to measure how many cell divisions a primed AP-1 chromatin state survives, and whether sister cells inherit priming concordantly. Heritability across mitosis plus sister concordance is taken as the operational definition of cellular memory and separates it from a long-lived but non-heritable cytoplasmic state.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracing across divisions
rewrites.description: Perform single-cell RNA and ATAC (multiome) on primed and naive cells, with barcode lineage tracing or sister-cell pairing after division, and infer AP-1 motif activity (e.g., chromVAR). Test whether sister cells share accessibility and AP-1 activity states more than random cells do, and whether memory is heritable through mitosis and bimodal versus graded.

rewrites.title: Live imaging of endogenous AP-1 reporters across divisions
rewrites.description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN and a target-gene reporter, then track mother-daughter lineages by time-lapse imaging to test whether activity states persist through mitosis and across generations. Pair this with mitotic CUT&RUN to test whether AP-1 bookmarks chromatin.

rewrites.title: Lag of chromatin state behind AP-1 occupancy after washout
rewrites.description: Track AP-1 (Fos/Jun, via HaloTag or CUT&RUN) and chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) through a time course after stimulus withdrawal. If accessibility and H3K27ac persist after AP-1 has left its sites, the chromatin state is retaining a record of prior AP-1 activity.

rewrites.title: Longitudinal AP-1 occupancy versus accessibility after washout
rewrites.description: Run CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors alongside ATAC-seq and H3K27ac at multiple time points after a transient stimulus to identify sites that stay open after AP-1 leaves. Persistence of accessibility without AP-1 would indicate that AP-1 acts as an initiator, with the memory held in chromatin state.

rewrites.title: Cis versus trans memory using two identical reporters
rewrites.description: Integrate two spectrally distinct but sequence-identical AP-1-responsive reporters at different genomic loci in the same cell and track both after a stimulus pulse. Locus-autonomous chromatin memory predicts that the two reporters decorrelate and decay independently, while cell-wide protein/feedback memory predicts that they remain tightly correlated. This separates the two mechanistic classes with one measurement.

rewrites.title: Synthetic AP-1 motif reporter series testing sufficiency
rewrites.description: Integrate at a single safe-harbor locus a library of reporters that systematically vary AP-1 motif number, affinity, spacing, and neighboring pioneer-factor motifs, then measure both acute induction and persistence after the stimulus ends. This tests whether AP-1 sites alone are sufficient to encode memory or only do so in specific sequence contexts, separating AP-1's inducer role from its memory role.
